rydberg.note: Extension to the schema. Excitation routes used in tweezer work: 5s5p 3P0 or 3P1 -> 5sns 3S1 (317-319 nm) and 5s2 1S0 -> 5s5p 1P1 -> 5sns 1S0 / 5snd 1D2 (461 + 413 nm). Quantum defect formula: delta(n) = d0 + d2/(n-d0)^2 + d4/(n-d0)^4, E_n = I_s - R/(n-delta)^2.

not_found: Measured reduced dipole matrix elements for Rydberg excitation (5s5p 3P0/3P1 -> 5sns 3S1 at 317-319 nm; 5s5p 1P1 -> 5sns 1S0 / 5snd 1D2 at 413 nm): searched Madjarov 2020, Couturier 2019, Ding 2018, DeSalvo 2016 and a web search; only Rabi frequencies for specific beam geometries are reported, no matrix element.
Measured 413 nm singlet Rydberg term energies: only the Rydberg-Ritz quantum defects compiled by Vaillant et al. 2012 were sourced.
Experimental branching fractions of 5s6s 3S1 to 3P0/3P1/3P2: only theoretical values (UDel portal, via Pucher et al.) located.
Measured A or matrix element of the 2.6 um 3P0-3D1 line and precise (better than NIST Ritz) frequency of that line: only the 3D1 lifetime (Nicholson 2015) and CI+all-order theory (Safronova 2013).
State-resolved measured lifetimes of 5s4d 3D2 and 3D3 (only term-averaged 2500(200) / 2900(200) ns and theory).
Measured A / lifetimes for 5s5d 3D and 5s6d 3D (497 / 483 / 487 / 403 / 394 nm lines) beyond the NIST ASD Aki values; no A values at all for the 403 nm 5s5p 3P2 - 5s6d 3D lines.
New measurements of the 481 / 487 nm lines (5s5p 3P - 5p2 3P, 3P1 - 5s5d 3D2): nothing beyond NIST ASD Aki located.
86-88 (and 84-88) isotope shifts of the 679, 688, 707 and 671 nm lines.
Hyperfine-resolved 87Sr shifts of the 461 nm line and hyperfine constants of 5s5d 1D2, 5s6s 1S0-adjacent and 5s6p states.
Measured Lande g_J factors of excited states (Pucher Table 4 values are calculated Lande values and were not copied).

notes: Conventions. (1) Isotope-shift keys 'a-b' mean nu(a) - nu(b), copied in the sign convention each source prints: '87-88' etc. from Pucher / Mickelson / Trautmann, '88-84' etc. from Stellmer & Schreck, Zhang, Patel. 87Sr shifts refer to the hyperfine centre of gravity. (2) Hyperfine B_MHz is the electric-quadrupole constant (called Q in the Boyd / Stellmer papers). (3) Fields beyond SCHEMA.md: other_values (competing measurements), reduced_matrix_element_ea0 (convention of the cited source; Pucher uses <J||er||J'> = sqrt(2J'+1)|d| with J' the upper level, Safronova uses the standard symmetric reduced element; the two agree numerically for these lines), line_strength_au, natural_linewidth_*, cascade_branching_to_3P, repump_efficiency, frequency_THz_other_isotopes, value_Hz_str / rel_unc for clock frequencies beyond double precision, unc_plus / unc_minus, type 'M2', and the top-level 'rydberg' block. (4) A_s for 679 / 688 / 707 nm are experimental 3S1 lifetime times THEORETICAL branching; the 5s4d 3D infrared A values and branchings are pure theory (Safronova 2013). (5) Conflicts are kept side by side in other_values: 707 nm 88Sr frequency of Pucher et al. (423.91634 THz) is about 2.8 GHz off the NIST Ritz value and looks like a sign error; 1P1 lifetime 5.216(14) vs 5.234(8) vs 5.263(4) ns; 1P1->1D2 rate 5.3(5)e3 (direct) vs 3.9(1.5)e3 (Hunter) vs 9.25(40)e3 s^-1 (theory); 461 nm frequency 650 503 815(6) vs 650 503 775(10) MHz; 87Sr 3P2-3D2 isotope shift, where Trautmann et al. point out that the literature 3P1-3D2 (+30.2(6) MHz) and 3P2-3D2 (+17(2) MHz) shifts imply a 3P2 shift of +75(2) MHz against their directly measured +62.91(4) MHz. (6) Patel's 483 nm frequency 620.25305(3) THz can be cross-checked against Stellmer's 3P2-5s5d 3D1 frequency plus the 3P0-3P2 interval from the 698 / 671 nm absolute frequencies, which gives about 620.253101 THz (my arithmetic, not a sourced number): 51 MHz lower.
